answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, switching primary vendors now risks a delivery disruption we cannot absorb (memory_c2's cost benefit doesn't address ramp/onboarding risk under tight capacity). Memory_c4 indicates renegotiating at renewal previously recovered real margin via benchmarking, which could help meet the 18% finance mandate without the integration/delivery risk of a vendor switch or the failure-mode complexity of adding a second source this cycle. I want to verify memory_c4's original record before committing, since it's the load-bearing precedent for believing negotiation alone can close a meaningful part of an aggressive 18% cut. Renewing outright (memory_c1) preserves stability but leaves cost pressure unaddressed, and deferring (memory_c5) was only validated for non-critical contracts, not one feeding a line at near-full committed volume. This is a single-cycle decision, so I'm not treating it as a full rollout of a new vendor relationship but as a targeted renegotiation with the incumbent, leaving second-sourcing or a vendor switch for the next review once more capacity buffer or clearer savings data exists.
